root_cause.text: The dpaa2-switch IRQ handler trusted the 16-bit if_id extracted from the hardware status register and used it directly as an index into the ethsw->ports[] array without validating it against sw_attr.num_ifs, allowing out-of-bounds access.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (if_id >= ethsw->sw_attr.num_ifs) { ... goto out; }` immediately before `port_priv = ethsw->ports[if_id];`, and the CVE/commit explicitly states that `if_id` can be any 16-bit value while `ports` is allocated with only `sw_attr.num_ifs` elements.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add validation of the IRQ-derived interface ID to prevent out-of-bounds port access in the switch interrupt handler.
intent_record.what: A bounds check was added after extracting if_id from the IRQ status: if if_id is greater than or equal to ethsw->sw_attr.num_ifs, the handler logs an error with dev_err() and jumps to the out label instead of accessing ethsw->ports[if_id].
intent_record.how: This prevents the IRQ handler from indexing the ports array with an invalid interface ID derived from the interrupt status, avoiding out-of-bounds access and safely aborting processing for malformed or unexpected IRQ data.

grouping_result.intent: Add validation of the IRQ-derived interface ID to prevent out-of-bounds port access in the switch interrupt handler.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause by validating the IRQ-derived interface ID before using it to index the ports array, preventing out-of-bounds access.

candidates.rationale: This directly uses the IRQ-derived if_id as an array index into ethsw->ports without validating it against the number of interfaces, causing the out-of-bounds access.
